scope: All Solidity sources below contracts/ except contracts/mocks/; npm dependencies are excluded.
policy: CI rejects every Critical signal and fails on every new, changed, or stale High signal. Entries document reviewed static-analysis signals; they are not blanket suppressions or claims that a source pattern is ideal.

findings.subject: BootstrapVault.finalise() arbitrary-send-erc20
findings.rationale: BootstrapVault V1 is deprecated. Its immutable ifrSource is constructor-configured, not caller-controlled; BootstrapVaultV3 is the finalized mainnet path.

findings.subject: BuybackController._addLiquidity(uint256) arbitrary-send-eth
findings.rationale: ETH is intentionally sent through the governance-configured Uniswap router and LP tokens go to the governance-configured lpReceiver. Neither destination is selected by execute() callers.

findings.subject: BuybackController._buybackAndBurn(uint256) arbitrary-send-eth
findings.rationale: ETH is intentionally sent through the governance-configured Uniswap router and purchased IFR is delivered to the immutable burnReserve. Neither destination is selected by execute() callers.

findings.subject: BuybackController.execute() reentrancy-eth
findings.rationale: The cooldown timestamp and execution counter are updated before external calls, blocking a nested execute(). The configured router remains an external trust boundary; add an explicit reentrancy guard in any future controller version.

findings.subject: BuybackController.withdrawIFR(address,uint256) unchecked-transfer
findings.rationale: The owner-only emergency path ignores the ERC-20 boolean return. Canonical IFR returns true or reverts, but a future controller should use SafeERC20 or require the returned value.

findings.subject: LendingVault.liquidate(uint256) arbitrary-send-eth
findings.rationale: The liquidator bonus is intentionally paid to msg.sender, the permissionless liquidate() caller. The function is nonReentrant and the recipient cannot be chosen independently of the caller.
